45.0.0.en: 1 “Thus saith the LORD to his anointed, to Cyrus, whose right hand I have holden, to subdue nations before him; and I will loose the loins of kings, to open before him the two leaved gates; and the gates shall not be shut; 2 I will go before thee, and make the crooked places straight: I will break in pieces the gates of brass, and cut in sunder the bars of iron: 3 And I will give thee the treasures of darkness, and hidden riches of secret places, that thou mayest know that I, the LORD, which call thee by thy name, am the God of Israel. 4 For Jacob my servant’s sake, and Israel mine elect, I have even called thee by thy name: I have surnamed thee, though thou hast not known me. 5 I am the LORD, and there is none else, there is no God beside me: I girded thee, though thou hast not known me: 6 That they may know from the rising of the sun, and from the west, that there is none beside me. I am the LORD, and there is none else. 7 I form the light, and create darkness: I make peace, and create evil: I the LORD do all these things. 8 Drop down, ye heavens, from above, and let the skies pour down righteousness: let the earth open, and let them bring forth salvation, and let righteousness spring up together; I the LORD have created it.”

45.0.1.en: It appears from the Babylonian writings that this Cyrus was the son of Cambyses and the grandson of another Cyrus, and that all of them, with their forefathers, reigned in the east of Elam, where Shushan was the capital of their kingdom from about the year 550 B.C.

45.0.2.en: Cyrus is considered the founder of the Persian kingdom. It is said that he began his life as the commander of an obscure troop in Persia, and succeeded in becoming the commander of two troops of mountain soldiers. He was extremely ambitious, so he began his conquests of the small neighboring kingdoms. Babylon, however, mocked him and made light of his abilities, until he entered Babylon in 539 B.C., in the days of Belshazzar its king, having gathered in his person the strength of the two kingdoms of Persia and Media. Thus the prophecy of Daniel was fulfilled (Dan 5:28), and Daniel was also in the court of Cyrus (Dan 6:28).

45.0.3.en: Herodotus and Xenophon (the young Greek) praised the person of Cyrus. The latter spoke of him, about 100 years after his death, as a supreme example of strength joined with simplicity, purity and self-control.

45.0.4.en: Now God addresses Cyrus about two centuries before his coming, declaring in it how He regards him, His divine work in his life, and God’s purpose for him. The following is observed in this address:

45.0.5.en: a. The word “I” of the Lord appears 16 times in God’s address to Cyrus [1-7], and 31 times in the whole chapter. It is as though God wants to affirm that the rise of Cyrus is by divine permission, and that his victory and that of his army, and the shattering of Babylon like an earthen vessel that cannot be mended, is from God Himself.

45.0.6.en: b. The Lord calls Cyrus “His anointed” [1], although he does not know the Lord [4-5]; perhaps because he worshiped the one unknown God while respecting religions as a whole, or because he fulfilled God’s plan for the deliverance of His people from the Babylonian captivity, and because he was a symbol of the Lord Christ, the Savior of the world.

45.0.7.en: c. Concerning God’s work with him, He says, “whose right hand I have holden, to subdue nations before him; and I will loose the loins of kings” [1]. God takes the role of the father who holds Cyrus as His child so that he may walk, as though God were his guide and the secret of his strength, upholding him to destroy evil. He gives him victory in the war against the nations so that he treads them down, since it was the custom for the victor to tread on the necks of the great men who were taken captive, and to loose the loins of kings, that is, to make them lose their strength and greatness, for kings used to wear exceedingly precious girdles as a sign of their greatness and might. This was fulfilled literally when King Belshazzar saw the fingers of a man’s hand writing on the wall of the palace: “the king’s countenance was changed, and his thoughts troubled him, so that the joints of his loins were loosed, and his knees smote one against another” (Dan 5:6).

45.0.8.en: In any case, Cyrus was a symbol of the Lord Christ in this matter, of whom it is said, “The Lord at thy right hand shall strike through kings in the day of his wrath” (Ps 110:5). It is said of Cyrus that the Lord held his right hand, and here it is said of the Son, the Word, “The Lord at thy right hand”; and, wonderfully, it is said in the same psalm on the tongue of the Father, “Sit thou at my right hand” (Ps 110:1). It is as though the Son is at the right hand of the Father (Ps 110:1) and the Father at the right hand of the Son (Ps 110:5)... For the right hand does not signify a position in place or a particular direction, but is a symbol of divine power and a sign of union and inseparability, since the two are one in divinity and one in power.

45.0.9.en: And as Cush broke kings in pieces, so the Lord Christ broke the kings who were ungrateful and who resisted the truth, for it is said: “shall strike through kings in the day of his wrath” (Ps 110:5). St. Augustine comments on this, saying: [These kings were wounded by His glory, and He made them weak by the weight of His name, so that they no longer had power to accomplish what they wished... They wished to blot out the Christian name from the face of the earth, but they could not, for whoever falls on this stone will be broken. The kings fell on this stone of stumbling and were wounded when they said: Who is Christ?!].

45.1.0.en: Perhaps by the kings He meant especially those who did not receive the Lord Christ (Jn 1:11), for it was fitting that they should unite with Him as the King of kings and so become kings, preachers and witnesses for Him. This is a matter that astonished the prophets when they prophesied about it, for Isaiah says in the same chapter, “Verily thou art a God that hidest thyself, O God of Israel, the Saviour” [15]; and the Apostle Paul was also astonished at it (Rom 10:20; 11:7; 9:30).

45.1.1.en: d. “To open before him the two leaved gates; and the gates shall not be shut” [1]. Thus God goes before Cyrus His anointed to open the closed gates before him, and the fortresses made by human hands collapse before him; even nature moves to support him: “I will go before thee, and make the crooked places straight: I will break in pieces the gates of brass, and cut in sunder the bars of iron” [2].

45.1.2.en: When we are joined to our victorious Christ, we walk in the royal way and rise toward heavenly things as though without hindrance, because the Lord goes before us, and the gates of eternity are opened before Him on our behalf. Cyrus stormed the walls of Babylon with their huge bronze gates, which numbered a hundred gates according to Herodotus.

45.1.3.en: e. God gives Cyrus the hidden treasures of Babylon, for it was the custom of kings to hide their treasures in places that no one knew, so that the enemy could not seize them.

45.1.4.en: “And I will give thee the treasures of darkness, and hidden riches of secret places, that thou mayest know that I, the LORD, which call thee by thy name, am the God of Israel” [3]. Since God is the “One who forms the light” [7], He reveals the hidden things to His children and grants them the treasures of His grace that cannot be comprehended.

45.1.5.en: f. God reveals to Cyrus His purpose for him: “For Jacob my servant’s sake, and Israel mine elect, I have even called thee by thy name: I have surnamed thee, though thou hast not known me” [5]. What He gives him is given on behalf of His believers and for the sake of His people... Thus it is fitting for us, as anointed ones of the Lord, to cling to our unique Lord Jesus Christ, and to recognize our mission, which is the building up of the congregation and its growth in the Lord.

45.1.6.en: g. Since the Persian religions were known for the Gnosticism that focused on the “duality of God,” meaning the existence of a god of good and a god of evil, God wanted to remove this thought from Cyrus, saying to him: “I am the LORD, and there is none else; I form the light, and create darkness: I make peace, and create evil: I the LORD do all these things” [7].

45.1.7.en: The word “evil ra” has come not in the sense of sin, but the fruit of sin or its punishment, of sorrow and distress. St. John Chrysostom says: [There is an evil that is truly evil: adultery, debauchery, covetousness, and countless other hidden things that deserve severe rebuke and punishment. And there is also an evil that is in truth not evil, but is so called, such as famine, disaster, death, sickness and the like; for these are not evils, but are so called. Why? Because if they were evils they would not become a source of our good, since they discipline our pride and our sloth, lead us to zeal, and make us more watchful]. In the same sense Abba Theodore says in the Conferences of St. John Cassian: [Holy Scripture is accustomed to use the expressions “evils” and “sorrows” in improper senses, for they are not evil in their nature, but are so called because they are thought to be evils by those to whom they have not brought good].

45.2.s.en: 2. Murmuring against the choice of Cyrus:

45.2.0.en: 9 “Woe unto him that striveth with his Maker! Let the potsherd strive with the potsherds of the earth. Shall the clay say to him that fashioneth it, What makest thou? or thy work, He hath no hands? 10 Woe unto him that saith unto his father, What begettest thou? or to the woman, What hast thou brought forth? 11 Thus saith the LORD, the Holy One of Israel, and his Maker, Ask me of things to come concerning my sons, and concerning the work of my hands command ye me. 12 I have made the earth, and created man upon it: I, even my hands, have stretched out the heavens, and all their host have I commanded. 13 I have raised him up in righteousness, and I will direct all his ways: he shall build my city, and he shall let go my captives, not for price nor reward, saith the LORD of hosts.”

45.2.1.en: It appears that murmuring arose among the Jews and also among the Gentiles. The Jews murmured against God because He accomplishes salvation by a pagan man, for his choice shatters their pride and their zeal for their own kind. This was on the part of the Jews; as for the Gentiles, the soul of some of them was embittered that one of them should take this role, accomplishing for the Jews deliverance from captivity and helping to establish the rites in Jerusalem.

45.2.2.en: In the face of this situation Isaiah lifted his heart toward God to offer a liturgical prayer, declaring in it that what takes place through Cyrus is a symbol of what is accomplished by the Lord Christ. It is as though he were asking the Jews as well as the Gentiles to turn from their murmuring to the experience of the free salvation offered to all. This is what moved Isaiah to turn in his address from Cyrus to Christ, our righteousness and salvation, saying: “Drop down, ye heavens, from above, and let the skies pour down righteousness: let the earth open, and let them bring forth salvation, and let righteousness spring up together; I the LORD have created it” [8]. It is as though he were repeating what is in the Book of Psalms: “Surely his salvation is nigh them that fear him; that glory may dwell in our land. Mercy and truth are met together; righteousness and peace have kissed each other. Truth shall spring out of the earth; and righteousness shall look down from heaven, etc....” (Ps 85:9-13); “Then shall the earth yield her increase; and God, even our own God, shall bless us” (Ps 67:6); “The mountains shall bring peace to the people, and the little hills, by righteousness” (Ps 72:3)...

45.2.3.en: It is as though the prophet were repeating that salvation is accomplished not because of Cyrus, but through the salvation of the Lord Christ and His righteousness... In Him our peace is accomplished through the meeting of mercy with truth, or mercy with divine justice, for on the Cross He paid the price in full through His infinite righteousness.

45.2.4.en: St. Augustine sees that in Christ the Jews met with the Gentiles through the meeting of truth with mercy; for the Jews knew the truth through the Law and the prophecies, and the Gentiles received mercy after they left their idolatrous worship, and these met with those as one people, righteous and holy to the Lord.

45.2.5.en: In the Lord Christ heaven met with earth, for He, the heavenly Son of God, became the Son of man, and was born as a human being on our earth... Therefore the prophet says: “Drop down, ye heavens, from above, and let the skies pour down righteousness” [8], as though he were saying: “He bowed the heavens also, and came down” (Ps 18:9); the Righteous and Holy One came down as from His heavens to accomplish our salvation. As for his saying, “let the earth open, and let them bring forth salvation, and let righteousness spring up together” [8], it means: “Truth shall spring out of the earth” (Ps 85). And as St. Augustine says: [Christ was born of a woman; the Son of God became flesh. What is the truth? The Son of God! What is the earth? The flesh... But the Truth that sprang out of the earth was before the earth, for by Him the heavens and the earth were made; yet that righteousness might look down from heaven, that is, that human beings might be justified by divine grace, the Truth was born of the Virgin Mary, that He might offer a sacrifice that justifies them, the sacrifice of suffering, the sacrifice of the Cross].

45.2.6.en: After the prophet turned our eyes from Cyrus to Christ the Savior, through His unique sacrifice that is able to justify, he rebuked the Jews and the Gentiles for their murmuring against the Lord, presenting two woes:

45.2.7.en: a. The first woe: the potsherd entering into strife with the potter, and the clay with him who fashions it; for it is not the right of a piece of pottery to demand of its maker a particular form, as to say to him, “thy work, He hath no hands” [9]... that is, you made the pottery without hands.

45.2.8.en: b. The second woe: the child’s protest against his father and mother, “What begettest thou?” or “What hast thou brought forth?”... I wished that you had borne me an angel and not a human being who carries human weakness and comes under the burdens of earthly life and its troubles.

45.2.9.en: It is fitting for us, as pottery or as children, to thank our Maker and Father, not to murmur against Him!

45.3.0.en: 14 “Thus saith the LORD, The labour of Egypt, and merchandise of Ethiopia and of the Sabeans, men of stature, shall come over unto thee, and they shall be thine: they shall come after thee; in chains they shall come over, and they shall fall down unto thee, they shall make supplication unto thee, saying, Surely God is in thee; and there is none else, there is no God. 15 Verily thou art a God that hidest thyself, O God of Israel, the Saviour. 16 They shall be ashamed, and also confounded, all of them: they shall go to confusion together that are makers of idols. 17 But Israel shall be saved in the LORD with an everlasting salvation: ye shall not be ashamed nor confounded world without end. 18 For thus saith the LORD that created the heavens; God himself that formed the earth and made it; he hath established it, he created it not in vain, he formed it to be inhabited: I am the LORD; and there is none else. 19 I have not spoken in secret, in a dark place of the earth: I said not unto the seed of Jacob, Seek ye me in vain: I the LORD speak righteousness, I declare things that are right.”

45.3.1.en: The Jews, like the Gentiles, were occupied with the story of Cyrus in its letter and in his temporal works, although it was fitting for all to pierce through the letter and meet the hidden God who works behind history for the salvation of all. So in a fatherly rebuke the Lord says: “Ask me of things to come concerning my sons, and concerning the work of my hands command ye me” [11].

45.3.2.en: I would have you be occupied only with the things to come, that is, with the eternal future, where it is fitting for you to seek the Kingdom of God and His righteousness, and all these things shall be added to you. And that you pray for His sons, that is, that in our prayers we be occupied with His believers and the work of His hands, for it is fitting for us to realize our standing and our wonderful boldness before Him. In other words, our eternal Kingdom, our witness to others and our longing for the salvation of every human being, all these are matters more important than murmuring at Cyrus’s taking this role in their deliverance from the Babylonian captivity.

45.4.0.en: Once again He affirms to them that they must be occupied with Him and not with Cyrus, for He is “a God that hidest thyself... the Saviour” [15]; He is the One who works in secret.

45.4.1.en: The characteristics of this divine salvation are:

45.4.2.en: a. A free salvation: “I have raised him up in righteousness, and I will direct all his ways: he shall build my city, and he shall let go my captives, not for price nor reward, saith the LORD of hosts” [13]. Cyrus fulfilled God’s plan for His people without awaiting a reward from the people; they did not pay Cyrus a price for making the ways easy for them, building the city and freeing them from captivity. That was a symbol of the free salvation of the Lord Christ, as the Apostle Paul says: “Being justified freely by his grace through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus: Whom God hath set forth to be a propitiation through faith in his blood, to declare his righteousness for the remission of sins that are past, through the forbearance of God” (Rom 3:24-25).

45.4.3.en: b. A collective salvation: He turns the Egyptians, the Ethiopians and the Sabeans to faith, so that they enter the new Israel in a spirit of humility and worship [14]. Our Lord Jesus Christ stretched out His hands on the Cross to gather with one the old people and with the other the company of the Gentiles; He gathered the whole world into His embrace to raise humanity to sonship to the Father by His Holy Spirit.

45.5.0.en: c. An eternal salvation: “But Israel shall be saved in the LORD with an everlasting salvation: ye shall not be ashamed nor confounded world without end” [17].

45.6.0.en: d. A public salvation: “I have not spoken in secret, in a dark place of the earth” [19]. The Lord of glory was crucified openly on the hill of Golgotha.

45.7.s.en: 4. A call to salvation in Christ:

45.7.0.en: 20 “Assemble yourselves and come; draw near together, ye that are escaped of the nations: they have no knowledge that set up the wood of their graven image, and pray unto a god that cannot save. 21 Tell ye, and bring them near; yea, let them take counsel together: who hath declared this from ancient time? who hath told it from that time? have not I the LORD? and there is no God else beside me; a just God and a Saviour; there is none beside me. 22 Look unto me, and be ye saved, all the ends of the earth: for I am God, and there is none else. 23 I have sworn by myself, the word is gone out of my mouth in righteousness, and shall not return, That unto me every knee shall bow, every tongue shall swear. 24 Surely, shall one say, in the LORD have I righteousness and strength: even to him shall men come; and all that are incensed against him shall be ashamed. 25 In the LORD shall all the seed of Israel be justified, and shall glory.”

45.7.1.en: The Lord Christ speaks to the Gentiles to call them to enjoy Him as a Savior able to justify them. “Assemble yourselves and come; draw near together, ye that are escaped of the nations... Look unto me, and be ye saved, all the ends of the earth: for I am God, and there is none else. I have sworn by myself, the word is gone out of my mouth in righteousness, and shall not return, That unto me every knee shall bow, every tongue shall swear. Surely, shall one say, in the LORD have I righteousness and strength: even to him shall men come; and all that are incensed against him shall be ashamed. In the LORD shall all the seed of Israel be justified, and shall glory” [20-24].

45.7.2.en: It is observed in this call:

45.7.3.en: a. A collective call, in which He asks the Gentiles to gather together as one holy Church, coming forward in the spirit of the community to receive His work of salvation.

45.7.4.en: b. God is the Savior and there is no other, as the Apostle Paul says: “For it became him, for whom are all things, and by whom are all things, in bringing many sons unto glory, to make the captain of their salvation perfect through sufferings” (Heb 2:10). And as Pope Athanasius the Apostolic says: [By these words he means that it was not the place of anyone else to bring human beings back from what they had begun, except the Word of God, who also made them from the beginning... For by the sacrifice of His body He put an end to the decree that was against us, for just as death reigned over human beings through a man, so also through the Word of God, when He became man, death was destroyed and the resurrection of life began].

45.7.5.en: c. A call full of hope, which achieves its aim in that every knee shall bow to Him.

45.7.6.en: d. A call whose foundation is faith: “Look unto me,” as the old people believed before and looked at the bronze serpent and were healed.

45.7.7.en: e. The enjoyment of the righteousness and power of the Savior.

45.7.8.en: f. The Savior is the secret of the glory of His believers and the shame of those who oppose Him.
